entrypoints.summary: The syzbot case exposes public C and syz reproducer assets for a filesystem-triggered kernel write-path crash; supplied case metadata identifies the observed path as a v9fs-backed unbuffered/direct write reaching netfs_unbuffered_write.

affected_components.role: Pre-fix retry logic conditionally reset and directly reissued a subrequest when prepare_write was absent.
KASAN reports the post-free read in this function at line 119; the fixed implementation removes the duplicate-reissue branch and updates progress/flag handling.

code_slices.fixed: The fix removes that else branch, accounts partial transfer in wreq->transferred, clears MADE_PROGRESS, and applies IN_PROGRESS/stat handling independently of callback presence.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The KASAN report identifies a read in netfs_unbuffered_write at direct_write.c:119 after netfs_subrequest release.
code_slices.vulnerable: Pre-fix retry handling reset the iterator and directly called netfs_reissue_write when stream->prepare_write was absent.

negative_controls: Run the same preserved reproducer against the fixed commit and check that this KASAN signature is absent; no direct execution transcript is independently asserted here.
observability.positive_marker: KASAN reports a slab use-after-free read in netfs_unbuffered_write at fs/netfs/direct_write.c:119.

preconditions: An affected pre-fix Linux kernel revision is used.
The filesystem/write path uses netfs unbuffered/direct write and reaches a retrying subrequest on a stream without prepare_write.
The supplied syzbot case records public repro assets, but their concrete contents are not preserved separately in this bundle.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Public syz/C repro is listed by the case; exact syscall sequence and bytes are unavailable in this materialized bundle.
trigger_steps.summary: Issue the case's applicable filesystem direct/unbuffered write so that the retry condition is reached for a stream without prepare_write.

mitigations.concept: single-loop retry lifecycle with progress accounting

relation_candidates.rationale: The pre-fix branch for streams without prepare_write resets and reissues a write; the commit explicitly identifies duplicate write issuance in this condition.

The patch removes duplicate reissue for this reported UAF, while the crash report records the subsequent freed-subrequest read; full ownership sequencing remains incompletely represented in the bundle.
KASAN directly reports a size-2 slab use-after-free read in netfs_unbuffered_write.

relation_candidates.dst: single-loop retry lifecycle with progress accounting
relation_candidates.rationale: The committed fix deletes reset/reissue in the no-callback branch and adds progress and flag-state updates while retaining IN_PROGRESS handling.

impact.affected_asset: Kernel netfs subrequest memory and stability of the affected filesystem write path.
impact.attacker_capability: A local process able to drive the applicable filesystem direct/unbuffered write and retry condition can trigger the demonstrated kernel fault under the recorded reproducer environment.
impact.security_effect: Kernel slab use-after-free read detected by KASAN; the supplied evidence establishes a memory-safety crash, not exploitation.

causal_trace.summary: A direct/unbuffered filesystem write reaches the netfs retry path with a subrequest needing retry; the affected condition is a stream without a prepare_write callback.

Before the fix, the no-prepare_write retry branch reset the subrequest iterator and called netfs_reissue_write, even though returning to the surrounding loop repeats the required retry work; the upstream commit describes this as re-issuing a write twice.

After subrequest release through netfs_put_subrequest/netfs_free_subrequest, netfs_unbuffered_write reads subrequest state at fs/netfs/direct_write.c:119; KASAN reports this as a size-2 read of freed slab memory.
The reproduced outcome is a KASAN-detected slab use-after-free read in netfs_unbuffered_write, yielding a kernel memory-safety crash report.

failure.operation: Read of freed netfs_subrequest state in netfs_unbuffered_write (KASAN size-2 read at fs/netfs/direct_write.c:119)

primary_invariant.statement: A retry of an unbuffered/direct write must have one coherent retry lifecycle: partial progress is accounted for, retry flags are transitioned consistently, and a no-prepare_write stream must not independently reset and reissue work already performed by the retry loop.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-fix no-callback branch invoked netfs_reset_iter and netfs_reissue_write in addition to loop-driven retry processing, causing a write to be issued twice; the reported crash subsequently observes a read after the subrequest was freed.

quality.review_notes: The dashboard records public reproducer availability, a KASAN allocation/free/use oracle, and successful patch-test context, while the exact repro bodies and configuration are not separately materialized in this bundle. The causal connection from duplicate reissue to the precise asynchronous release/read sequence is patch- and crash-backed but not fully reconstructed from broader netfs ownership helpers. No conclusion about exploitability, remote reachability, or privilege escalation is made.

remediation.invariant_restored: The fix removes the no-prepare_write iterator-reset/direct-reissue branch, updates wreq->transferred for partial transfer, clears MADE_PROGRESS, and sets IN_PROGRESS outside the callback conditional, leaving the retry loop as the coherent reprocessing path.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Drive an applicable direct/unbuffered write through a filesystem stream without prepare_write such that the subrequest enters the retry path; exact reproducer contents are not materialized.
data_structure_invariants: wreq->transferred must include a partial subrequest transfer before further retry processing.
NETFS_SREQ_MADE_PROGRESS must be cleared on retry transition.
A no-prepare_write branch must not separately reissue work that the enclosing retry loop will perform.
Subrequest state must not be read after its ownership/reference lifecycle has released it.
state_context.state_machine: A write subrequest enters retry processing; the affected pre-fix path diverges based on whether stream->prepare_write exists. The corrected path leaves reprocessing to the enclosing loop while explicitly updating request progress and retry-related flags.

oracle.expected_negative: After applying fix commit 64f04f9789237728be4e1836151848af350d1374, the same crash signature should not be reported by the recorded patch-test context.
